newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH OCT PAPER EXPORTS DOWN 26 PCT YR/YR - NCB.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH OCT PAPER EXPORTS DOWN 26 PCT YR/YR - NCB.

text.p: The value of Finnish paper exports fell 26 percent year-on-year in October after falling 22 percent in September, the National Customs Board (NCB) said on Friday.
In the broader paper, pulp and paperboard category, the value of October exports fell 18 percent after a 21 percent decline in September.
In January-October, paper, pulp and paperboard exports were 12 percent lower year-on-year at 36.31 billion markka, or 24.3 percent of total Finnish exports in the first 10 months, NCB said.
Wood industry exports fell one percent in October for an aggregate 10-month fall of 10 percent to 10.23 billion markka, or 6.9 percent of Finnish January-October exports.
In the metal products and machinery industry the value of exports turned into a two percent year-on-year fall in October after a six percent increase in September and an 11 percent climb in August.
In January-October, metal products and machinery industry exports were 12 percent up on the year-ago period at 61.60 billion markka -- 41.3 percent of the total.
The value of basic metal industry exports fell 20 percent in October after falling 17 percent in September, NCB said.
In January-October, Finnish basic metals exports were flat at 11.71 billion markka, or 7.9 percent of all January-October exports.

Exports of chemical industry products rose 20 percent in October after a 10 percent rise in September. In the first 10 months of 1996, chemicals exports were 13 percent higher at 15.17 billion markka, accounting for 10.2 percent of the total.
Overall, Finnish October exports fell four percent year-on-year while January-October exports were three percent higher than in the corresponding period inm 1995, NCB said.
